stem.text: A function f has derivative \( f'(x) = -3\left(x + 3\right)\left(x + 2\right) \) for all real x. On what open intervals is f decreasing? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -3) \) and \( (-2, \infty) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.

worked_solution.text: The sign of f' can change only where \( f'(x) = 0 \) at \( x = -3 \) and \( x = -2 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: partition points of the sign chart

worked_solution.text: Testing one point in each piece gives \( f'(x) < 0 \) on the intervals \( (-\infty, -3) \) and \( (-2, \infty) \) and \( f'(x) > 0 \) on the interval \( (-3, -2) \).
So f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -3) \) and \( (-2, \infty) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction of the function

options.label: f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -3) \) and \( (-2, \infty) \), because it is negative there.
options.derivation: the right intervals, justified by a pronoun that never says which function is positive or negative
